cards: **ml-ensemble-extremes · Ensemble size for rare extremes in a machine-learned weather ensemble.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: the lever · PASS **Question.** Does 10 to 1,000 AIFS-ENS members beat 50 for top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain probability forecasts, or does shared model error cap the skill? **What is known.** HENS Part 2: 7,424 SFNO members per day for 92 summer-2023 dates; showed huge ensembles sample 4-sigma tails and reduce outliers. Whether AIFS-ENS, whose members are exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution, keeps gaining skill past 50 members or saturates from shared model error. **Hypothesis.** More members keep helping: 1,000 members sample top-percentile tails far better than 50, so extreme-event scores keep improving [s_hens]. **If compute is the lever.** Skill on top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain keeps rising past 50 members: 1,000 members sharpen the tails and improve extreme-event scores. **If not.** Skill flattens near 50 members: members are exchangeable draws of one trained distribution, so shared model error caps tail sharpness and extra members add nothing. **Test.** Run 7,000 fifteen-day AIFS-ENS v1 forecasts (7 dates x 1,000 members) on eight A100 40 GB GPUs; subsample 10-1,000 members, score top-percentile wind/temperature/rain probabilities against ERA5 with fair CRPS and Brier scores, and test whether skill still rises past 50 members. *Compute axis.* Ensemble members per forecast: 10–1,000 members, 6 levels. Closest prior: 7,424 [s_hens], not beyond it. *Restructuring.* none. **Check first.** Reproduce the published 4-minute N320 member time and 38 GB memory; one control run must match ECMWF open data within ensemble spread [s_crps_paper]. Tolerance: timing within +/-25% of 4 min; 38 GB memory fits; control field within the ensemble's own member-to-member spread at each lead time (GPUs are non-deterministic, so exact reproduction is not expected). **Would not show.** Applies to AIFS-ENS v1 medium-range extremes on 7 dates; not a multi-season reforecast, other models, subseasonal leads, or direct proof that shared error causes any saturation. *Cost.* Plans $963.17 of the $1,000 budget over 74.3 machine-hours, leaving $36.83. Main guess: peak filesystem usage [g], measured after $19.90 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 15× higher. Full scale: A 30-date multi-season reforecast at 1,000 members, $3,980, 3.98× the budget. **Judges.** Dramaturg: PASS 2/2.
